skill.name: grasshopper-workflow
skill.description: Automates Grasshopper parametric modeling through MCP by creating components, wiring connections, setting parameters, grouping elements, and generating workflow files.

security_audit.summary: The confirmed issues are limited to unrestricted local file writes that can overwrite caller-selected paths. The reconnaissance, dynamic import, external command, and obfuscation alerts are false positives from Grasshopper IDs, markdown fences, static imports, Chinese documentation, and GUID examples. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration intent, or malicious control flow was found.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve output paths under a workspace such as GH_WIP, reject traversal, and confirm before overwriting existing files.
Write updates to a temporary file first, keep a backup, then replace the target file after validation succeeds.
Document that commands should target a trusted local Grasshopper MCP server unless the user explicitly approves a remote host.

content.value_statement: Grasshopper workflows often require repeated component creation, connection setup, parameter entry, and result checking. This skill organizes those steps into MCP-driven scripts, CLI actions, and workflow files for repeatable parametric modeling.
actual_capabilities: Creates Grasshopper components through a local MCP server using GUID, X position, and Y position inputs.
Connects components by source and target IDs, with optional source and target parameter names.
Parses component_info.mmd files to extract components, connections, subgraphs, and slider values.
Generates placement_info.json workflow files from parsed MMD component and connection data.
Sets Number Slider and Vector XYZ values, including automatic slider range selection.
Creates component groups with names and RGB or hex colors.
limitations: Requires a running Grasshopper MCP server, usually on localhost port 8080.
Does not validate every Grasshopper GUID against an official catalog before execution.
Can overwrite output files when commands are given existing paths.
Workflow examples focus on structured MMD and placement_info.json inputs.

use_cases.title: Build Parametric Furniture Models
use_cases.description: Create repeatable Grasshopper component graphs for tables, legs, sliders, surfaces, and final boolean operations.

use_cases.title: Convert Design Diagrams Into Workflows
use_cases.description: Parse MMD component diagrams into placement workflows that can be checked, executed, and refined.

use_cases.title: Standardize Grasshopper Automation
use_cases.description: Use CLI commands to generate, execute, inspect, and group Grasshopper workflow files in a consistent process.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use grasshopper-workflow to help me define a simple parametric table. Ask for missing dimensions before creating workflow files.

prompt_templates.title: Parse Existing Diagram
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my component_info.mmd and identify missing GUIDs, component positions, and connection issues before generating placement steps.

prompt_templates.title: Execute Placement Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a prepared Grasshopper placement workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Grasshopper placement workflow from GH_WIP/placement_info.json. Save the component ID map and report failed components or connections.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Repair Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect document errors, compare slider values with component_info.mmd, repair incorrect connections, then group related components by subsystem.

output_examples.input: A request to create a parametric table with width, length, height, and four legs.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow with clarified dimensions, component groups, slider values, and a placement file ready for review.

output_examples.input: An existing component_info.mmd file with missing component GUIDs.
output_examples.output: A checklist of unresolved components, suggested GUID lookup steps, and placement updates to complete before execution.

output_examples.input: A completed placement workflow that produced connection errors.
output_examples.output: An execution summary showing failed connections, likely parameter mismatches, and the next repair actions.

best_practices: Keep workflow files inside GH_WIP or another dedicated project folder.
Review generated placement_info.json before executing component creation.
Run get-errors after placement and fix failed connections before grouping components.
anti_patterns: Do not run placement files from untrusted sources without inspecting commands.
Do not point the MCP client at remote hosts unless you control the server.
Do not use broad output paths that can overwrite unrelated project files.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Grasshopper component creation, connection setup, parameter setting, grouping, and placement workflow execution through MCP.

faq.question: Does it require Rhino or Grasshopper?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects a running Grasshopper MCP server, usually available on localhost port 8080.

faq.question: What files does it use?
faq.answer: It works with component_info.mmd, part_info.mmd, placement_info.json, and component_id_map.json workflow files.

faq.question: Can it generate placement_info.json?
faq.answer: Yes. It parses MMD component and connection data, then creates a placement workflow file.

faq.question: Can it modify existing files?
faq.answer: Yes. Some commands write output files or update JSON files, so review paths before execution.

faq.question: Is it useful without MCP access?
faq.answer: Only partly. Parsing and planning can work offline, but execution requires Grasshopper MCP connectivity.
